title: Food Delivery Service: Complete Architecture
description: Design a 3-sided marketplace food delivery platform (DoorDash / Uber Eats) with order orchestration, dynamic driver dispatch, and real-time tracking.

data.text: Design a three-sided on-demand food delivery platform like DoorDash or Uber Eats connecting Customers, Restaurants (Merchants), and Delivery Couriers (Dashers). The platform handles 10+ million daily orders with sharp dinner and lunch spikes. The engineering complexity lies in coordinating physical world logistics: synchronizing food kitchen prep time with driver arrival to avoid cold food, real-time geospatial matching, route optimization with multi-order batching, and an auditable order lifecycle state machine across all three parties.

terms.definition: A business ecosystem coordinating three distinct stakeholders simultaneously: Consumer (demand), Restaurant (supplier), and Courier (fulfillment).
Dispatching a courier such that their estimated travel time aligns precisely with the kitchen's estimated food preparation completion time.
Assigning multiple delivery drop-offs to a single driver if pickups originate from the same or neighboring restaurants and routes align.
A strictly coordinated workflow: PLACED -> MERCHANT_ACCEPTED -> PREPARING -> COURIER_ASSIGNED -> AT_RESTAURANT -> PICKED_UP -> DELIVERED.
Hexagonal spatial partitioning to enforce restaurant delivery boundaries and calculate localized supply-demand metrics.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Customer: Search nearby restaurants by cuisine/distance, browse dynamic menus, place orders, and track deliveries on live maps
Merchant (Restaurant): Accept/reject incoming orders, update estimated prep times, and mark out-of-stock items in real-time
Courier (Driver): Receive dispatch offers, accept deliveries, get turn-by-turn routing, and submit proof-of-delivery photos
Dynamic Dispatch Engine: Match available couriers to ready orders minimizing customer ETA and driver idle wait time
Live Tracking: Stream courier GPS coordinates to the customer application every 3-5 seconds
Payment & Settlement: Split customer payment into restaurant revenue, courier fee/tips, and platform commission

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Scale: 10M+ daily orders; 250,000 peak concurrent active deliveries; 500,000 active couriers
Order Placement Latency: <500ms P99 order confirmation with strict idempotency
Tracking Freshness: Driver location displayed on customer map within 3 seconds of GPS emission
State Consistency: 100% strict ordering of fulfillment state transitions (zero lost or dangling orders)
Availability: 99.99% for customer checkout and restaurant order ingest

data.text: The platform coordinates three distinct client interfaces through a unified API Gateway, orchestrating the physical delivery through a stateful Fulfillment SAGA and a Geospatial Dispatch Engine.

data.text: To ensure food arrives hot, the dispatch engine delays offering the delivery to couriers until the kitchen has accepted and began preparation, timing driver arrival within 2 minutes of the food bagging.

faqs.question: Why is greedy dispatch bad for food delivery?
faqs.answer: In ride-sharing (Uber), the passenger is ready on the curb immediately, so dispatching the nearest car is optimal. In food delivery, food requires 15-30 minutes of cooking. Dispatching the nearest driver immediately means the driver stands idle in the kitchen for 20 minutes, wasting driver earning hours and increasing churn. Just-in-Time dispatch coordinates driver arrival with food completion.

faqs.question: How do you handle restaurant out-of-stock items after the customer has paid?
faqs.answer: The Order Orchestrator supports pre-authorized item substitution preferences: (1) Substitute with closest match, (2) Call/text customer for 5-minute decision window, or (3) Refund and proceed with remaining items. The payment pre-authorizes the total cart value with a 15% buffer, and the final payment settlement occurs when the food is picked up.

faqs.question: How does live driver GPS tracking scale to 500,000 concurrent couriers?
faqs.answer: Drivers emit coordinates over UDP/HTTP every 3 seconds to a Location Ingestion Service that updates Redis GEO keys with a 10-second TTL. The Customer App only listens to tracking coordinates when the order status is `PICKED_UP`. A WebSocket Gateway subscribes to the specific driver channel on Redis Pub/Sub, streaming coordinates only to that customer, preventing global broadcast storms.

faqs.question: How are multi-order batches (bundles) determined?
faqs.answer: The dispatch engine computes vehicle routing problem (VRP) constraints with strict time penalties: (1) The second order must not delay the first customer by more than 8-10 minutes, (2) The restaurants must be within 500 meters of each other, and (3) The delivery destinations must share the same directional corridor.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Food delivery is a 3-sided marketplace balancing consumer hunger, kitchen prep, and courier transit
Just-in-Time (JIT) dispatch coordinates driver arrival with kitchen cooking completion to keep food hot
Order state machine strictly enforces atomic transitions across all three client applications
Driver GPS streams are filtered and routed only to customers with active in-flight deliveries
Batching and bundling algorithms group nearby restaurant pickups heading in the same route corridor
data.takeaway: Food delivery systems succeed by mastering the interplay between kitchen preparation timing and geospatial courier logistics, transforming real-world delays into predictable, synchronized delivery flows.
